exposure: leaving the placenta in situ for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) management
outcome: time to expulsion or resorption (of placenta)
cohort: The study included 43 patients with antenatally diagnosed placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) who were managed by leaving the placenta in situ at a single center.
finding: The majority of patients with PAS managed by leaving the placenta in situ did not experience complications like infection or bleeding necessitating hysterectomy, and successful uterine preservation was associated with lower estimated total blood loss and transfusion rates compared to those undergoing interval hysterectomy.
